questions.q: In a solid lattice, the cation has left a lattice site and is located at an interstitial position, the lattice defect is :
questions.solution: Frenkel defect is due to dislocation of ion from its usual lattice site to interstitial position.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: Frenkel and Schottky defects are crystal defects. It arises due to dislodgement of cation or anion from their places in the crystal lattice.

questions.solution: Anti-fluorite structure refers to an anion array with tetrahedral cations and the compound having $A_2 B$ formula have anti-fluorite structure. So, $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{O}$ has an anti-fluorite structure in which $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ ions occupy all the tetrahedral voids and $\mathrmO^{2-}$ occupy half of the cubic holes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Element 'B' forms ccp structure and 'A' 'occupies half of the octahedral voids, while oxygen atoms occupy all the tetrahedral voids. The structure of bimetallic oxide is :
questions.solution: No. of lattice points $=$ No. of octahedral voids $=\frac{1}{2} \times$ No. of tetrahedral voids in $c c p$ structure $\therefore$ No. of atoms of $B=4$ No. of atoms of $A=\frac{1}{2} \times$ No. of octahedral voids $=\frac{1}{2} \times 4=2$ No. of atoms of $O=$ All tetrahedral voids $=2 \times$ No. of lattice points $=2 \times 4=8$ Hence, $A: B: O=1: 2: 4$ Therefore, the formula of the compound is $A B_{2} O_{4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a compound, atoms of elements $Y$ form ccp lattice and those of element $X$ occupy $2 / 3rd$& of& tetrahedral voids. The formula of the compound can be
questions.solution:
Let atoms of $Y$ in ccp structure $= 100$

Then, number of tetrahedral voids $= 2 \times 100$

$∵$ Number of $X$ atoms $= \dfrac{2}{3}$ rd of tetrahedral voids

$∴$ Number of $X$ atoms $= \dfrac{2}{3} \times 200 = \dfrac{400}{3}$

Hence, formula of compound can be $= {X}_{4}{Y}_{3}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metallic element has a cubic lattice. Each edge of the unit cell is $2\overset{.}{A}$ and the density of metal is $25g{cm}^{3}$. The unit cell in $200g$ of metal are
questions.solution:
Edge length of the unit cell $= 2\overset{.}{A} = 2 \times {10}^{- 8}cm$

Volume of unit cell $= \left(2 \times {10}^{- 8}\right)^{3} = 8 \times {10}^{- 24}{cm}^{3}$

Mass of one unit cell $=$ volume $\times$ density

$= 8 \times {10}^{- 24} \times 25$

Number of unit cell in $200g$ of metal

$= \dfrac{ mass of the metal }{ mass of one unit cell }$

$= \dfrac{200}{8 \times {10}^{- 24} \times 25} = 1 \times {10}^{24}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following, which have highest melting point?
questions.solution:
Ionic solids are formed by three dimensional arrangements of positive charged ions i.e. cations and negative charged ions i.e. anions. These ions are held together by coulombic(electrostatic) forces and hence, ionic solids are hard and brittle.

Ionic solids have highest melting point due to strong electrostatic force of attraction.

questions.q: The fraction of total volume occupied by the atoms present in a simple cube is
questions.solution:
Number of atoms per unit cell $=1$ Atoms touch each other along edges. Hence $r=\frac{a}{2}(\mathrm{r}=$ radius of atom and $\mathrm{a}=$ edge length)
Therefore $\%=\frac{\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}}{(2 r)^{3}}=\frac{\pi}{6}$
